task.description:
Validate src/design/iss0169-lua08-09-10-limiter-wiring.md (commit 360560a) before BACKEND-DEV implements it. ORCH has already independently spot-checked this design's most load-bearing technical claims against real source (not just trusted the CODE-DESIGNER report):
- host_context.zig's installContext/contextFromState functions genuinely use LUA_REGISTRYINDEX + lua_setfield/lua_getfield + lua_type guard + lua_pop(L,1) -- confirmed by direct read, matches the design's §1.2 claim field-for-field.
- instruction_limiter.zig's CURRENT installHook genuinely uses lua_setglobal(L, "__limiter__") (script-writable global) and is called from NO code path in executor.zig -- confirmed, matches design §1.1's defect claim.
- luajit_bindings.zig genuinely declares lua_sethook(L, f, mask, count) c_int, LUA_MASKCOUNT=8, LUA_TLIGHTUSERDATA=2, lua_newstate(f: lua_Alloc, ud) -- all signatures the design assumes are real, not invented.
- memory_limiter.zig's MemoryLimiter.init and timeout.zig's TimeoutContext.init genuinely do not allocate (confirmed by reading both) -- matches design §3.4's claim used to justify no new error variant.
- manifest.zig's Limits struct genuinely has MIN_INSTRUCTIONS=1_000, MAX_INSTRUCTIONS=10_000_000, MIN_MEMORY_BYTES=1_048_576, MIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1 -- confirmed, matches every numeric value the design cites in §3.2 and its test specs.
- executor.zig genuinely has createSandboxedState, executeScript, executeScriptWithManifest, executeSource, createState, defaultAlloc, and errors.LuaError.LuaAllocFailed already exists as an error variant -- confirmed, the design's §4.2 replacement plan targets real, existing code.

This pre-verification does NOT substitute for your own independent review -- run your own full check per your standard procedure (lint_design_artefact.py, acceptance-criteria coverage against all 3 requirements, confirm no implementation code beyond illustrative Type E signatures, confirm scope discipline against §8's explicit LUA-11/12/13/15/16 exclusion). python tools/lint_design_artefact.py src/design/iss0169-lua08-09-10-limiter-wiring.md already returns exit 0 (0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR) as of this handoff.

Pay particular attention to: (1) whether §2's combined LUA-08/LUA-10 hook design actually satisfies BOTH requirements' acceptance criteria independently and testably (not just 'a hook fires'), (2) whether §3.2's policy decision for executeScript's unmanifested path is adequately justified and does not silently change behavior in an undocumented way for existing callers (LUA-04's tests), (3) whether the three test specs in §5 are genuinely mutation-checkable as written (each includes an explicit 'what must happen if the wiring is reverted' check) or whether any is vague enough that a BACKEND-DEV implementation could satisfy the letter without the substance.
acceptance_criteria: Every LUA-08/09/10 acceptance criterion has a corresponding design element
No implementation code present beyond illustrative Type E signatures
All public function signatures listed and consistent with real source
Error taxonomy addressed (existing LuaError.LuaAllocFailed reused, no gaps)
Scope discipline: design does not reach into LUA-11/12/13/15/16
Combined hook design (§2) genuinely satisfies both LUA-08 and LUA-10 independently and testably
Three test specs (§5) are genuinely mutation-checkable, not just call-without-crash assertions

result.summary: src/design/iss0169-lua08-09-10-limiter-wiring.md fails validation on requirement coverage. lint_design_artefact.py exits 0, scope discipline against LUA-11/12/13/15/16 holds, all cited function signatures/constants/error-set claims verified against real source (host_context.zig, luajit_bindings.zig, manifest.zig, errors.zig, instruction_limiter.zig, memory_limiter.zig, timeout.zig, executor.zig), and the LUA-08/LUA-09 wiring plus the executeScript unmanifested-default-limits policy are sound and adequately justified. However LUA-10 acceptance criteria are only partially covered: the design's §2 combined lua_sethook count-hook can only interrupt Lua bytecode between VM instructions, so it structurally cannot satisfy LUA-10's first acceptance criterion ('a script that blocks on a host function is still terminable within the configured timeout') or its second ('the timeout is enforced from outside the Lua state') — a same-thread hook invoked BY the Lua VM is enforcement from inside, not outside. The design's own §2.1 quotes the prior lua-integration.md §15.1 language ('enforced by the host... not by Lua... even if a host function blocks') only to justify why the tight-loop case needs the hook, without acknowledging it has left the blocking-host-call and enforced-from-outside cases unaddressed. This is not flagged in §11 Open Questions (which claims none remain) and is not scoped out in §8. The pre-existing tests/specs/LUA-10.md already commits to exactly these two cases (TC-LUA-10-03 'host function call respects timeout', TC-LUA-10-04 'timeout enforced from outside Lua state'), and the design's own §5.3 TC-LUA-10-01 covers only the tight-loop sub-case (isolated from instruction count) while implicitly standing in as the requirement's complete test coverage. A BACKEND-DEV implementation built strictly to this design would satisfy the tight-loop half of LUA-10 and leave the blocking-host-call / host-enforced-from-outside half either unimplemented or, worse, silently reinterpreted as out of scope without that decision ever being surfaced for review.

issues.description: LUA-10 acceptance criterion 'A script that blocks on a host function is still terminable within the configured timeout' has no design element. §2's lua_sethook(L, hookCallback, LUA_MASKCOUNT, ...) count-hook fires only between Lua VM instruction dispatches; while a lua_CFunction such as platform.call_service is executing (blocking on real I/O once LUA-12 lands, or in principle any host_api/ function), the Lua VM is not dispatching instructions and the count hook cannot fire. The design must add a mechanism that can interrupt or bound a blocking host call (e.g. a genuine host-side timer/watchdog thread that can force termination independent of Lua's cooperation, or an explicit, reviewed decision to defer this sub-case to a later tranche with sign-off from ORCH given the requirement's MUST priority) -- it cannot be silently absorbed into the tight-loop hook design.

LUA-10 acceptance criterion 'The timeout is enforced from outside the Lua state' has no design element. The §2 hookCallback runs on the same OS thread and same call stack as the Lua VM, invoked BY lua_sethook's own dispatch loop -- this is enforcement from inside the Lua state's execution, not from outside it. The design must either implement genuinely external enforcement (a real watchdog independent of Lua callback cooperation) or explicitly re-scope/re-word this acceptance criterion via the proper requirement-change channel (REQ-ANALYST/REQ-VALIDATOR), not reinterpret it silently inside a wiring design.

§11 'Open Questions' states 'None. All decisions required by the acceptance criteria... are resolved above,' but the blocking-host-call and enforced-from-outside sub-cases of LUA-10 are neither resolved nor flagged as an open question -- they are omitted without acknowledgment. Per this design's own §8 scope-discipline principle ('If implementation discovers that ... the scope boundary was drawn wrong ... that must be escalated to ORCH before proceeding, not silently absorbed'), the same standard should have applied to this gap before the design reached validation.

tests/specs/LUA-10.md (pre-existing, already committed) contains TC-LUA-10-03 ('host function call respects timeout') and TC-LUA-10-04 ('timeout enforced from outside Lua state'), both integration/unit tests mapped directly to LUA-10's two literal acceptance criteria. The design's §5.3 TC-LUA-10-01 is presented as the LUA-10 test coverage for this tranche but does not correspond to either pre-existing spec's scenario -- it only covers a rename/subset of the pre-existing TC-LUA-10-02/TC-LUA-10-08 tight-loop scenario. The design does not reconcile this gap against the existing test spec inventory.

result.next_action: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER for rework: add a genuinely external enforcement mechanism for LUA-10's blocking-host-call and enforced-from-outside-the-Lua-state acceptance criteria (or escalate to ORCH/REQ channel if those criteria are to be re-scoped), and reconcile §5.3 test coverage against the pre-existing tests/specs/LUA-10.md TC-LUA-10-03/04 scenarios.
